lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The code portfolio link should be verified as a complete, working URL that leads directly to relevant work.
The linked repositories should have concise descriptions or documentation if they are not publicly understandable.
The date of birth should be removed.
items.because: It is irrelevant to technical hiring and can create unnecessary bias or privacy concerns.

items.says: The nationality should be removed.
items.because: It does not strengthen candidacy and is usually not requested on North American resumes.

items.says: The degree could include a relevant specialization, thesis, or coursework.
items.because: It should be added only if it provides information not already demonstrated in experience.

items.says: The overlap between the M.S. program and internship may need clarification as full-time, part-time, or structured around employment.
items.because: The overlapping dates may raise questions.

items.says: The degree could include genuinely competitive honors, GPA, or relevant coursework if space permits.
The location format should be standardized with the other entries.
items.because: “Metro City, USA” and “Metro City, Country” look inconsistent.

items.says: The meaning of “accuracy” should be specified with a named metric or diagnostic success measure.
items.because: Accuracy can mean many things.

items.says: The 35% improvement needs a clear comparison point or baseline.
items.because: The improvement is difficult to assess without a baseline.

items.says: The size and nature of the evaluation data should be clarified.
The bullet should give more emphasis to the business or model outcome than to technical details.
items.because: The tool-use and loss-masking details are currently more prominent than the outcome.

items.says: “Reviewer disagreement” should be defined more precisely.
items.because: The reader needs to understand what disagreement means.

items.says: The bullet should state whether the reduction was measured on held-out data, production cases, or an internal audit.
The effects of signal routing on recall, coverage, or latency should be clarified.
items.because: The routing may have introduced tradeoffs.

items.says: The sentence is dense and should make the roles of the three specialists and reviewer immediately clear.
“Equal accuracy” should be defined with the evaluation metric used.
items.because: The credibility of the result depends on a clearly controlled comparison.

items.says: The latency comparison should identify exactly what kind of SFT or production baseline was used.
items.because: The comparison point is not fully clear.

items.says: The number of cases or rollouts used in the comparison should be included if available.
The reward-design detail should be reduced unless it is central to the role.
items.because: The combination of training, reward, tool-call, latency, and accuracy details is information-dense.

items.says: The scope of adoption should be clarified beyond whether the harness was used only by the immediate team.
The bullet should explain how the regressions were identified and whether they were prevented from release.
items.because: The practical consequence of catching the regressions is unclear.

items.says: The evaluation runtime, automation level, or number of test cases should be added if possible.
items.because: These details would make the engineering contribution more concrete.

items.says: The loss-masking work duplicates the technical detail in line 9.
items.because: It repeats the first bullet without adding a separate measurable accomplishment.

items.says: The bullet describes a method rather than a measured outcome.
The claim that loss masking improved faithfulness needs a measured result.
items.because: The review says not to claim improved faithfulness without supporting evidence.

items.says: The backlog accomplishment appears duplicated or potentially inconsistent with line 28.
items.because: Both bullets describe a backlog reduction involving 800+ sensor signals.

items.says: The bullet should clarify the candidate’s individual contribution versus the team’s contribution.
items.because: The impact must be tied clearly to the candidate’s work.

items.says: The method and baseline used to measure the 68% backlog reduction should be explained.
The Mobility Systems internship should be reduced from six bullets to four or five.
items.because: Six bullets is somewhat long, especially when two overlap.

items.says: The Mobility Systems bullets should put the strongest measurable production impacts first.
items.because: Bullets should be ordered by relevance and impact rather than work chronology.

items.says: The meaning of a “4x” memory reduction should be stated unambiguously.
items.because: It could mean reduction to one-quarter or a fourfold decrease.

items.says: The bullet should explain what the memory reduction enabled, such as larger batches, larger models, lower cost, or deployment on specific hardware.
items.because: The practical consequence is missing.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether BF16 used hardware-supported acceleration.
The bullet should state whether model quality remained unchanged.
items.because: The quality tradeoff is missing.

items.says: The workload, request volume, or endpoint involved in the latency reduction should be clarified.
items.because: Additional scope would make the optimization easier to judge.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the 200 ms build threshold applied to all relevant endpoints or only one.
Relevant correctness or freshness safeguards for the cache should be mentioned.
“Maintained” and “adds” have an inconsistent tense and grammatical agreement.
items.because: The grammar issue makes the line look less polished.

items.says: The bullet should clarify what the candidate personally changed in the pipeline rather than only saying it was maintained.
“Shortened release cycles to 3 days” needs a previous duration or clarification that cycles were standardized at three days.
The outcome of the automated regression checks should be quantified if they caught failures.
The connection between pipeline ownership, automation, and release speed should be made clearer.
items.because: The bullet currently mixes these elements without clearly connecting cause and effect.

items.says: The candidate’s role in designing the queue architecture versus implementing the migration should be clarified.
The operational effect should be quantified with measures such as recovery rate, delay reduction, incidents avoided, or queue volume.
items.because: The reliability and business impact are somewhat qualitative.

items.says: The bullet should explain how removal of the nightly backlogs was observed or measured.
The “Owner” title should be verified as an accurate description of the role.
The project should be verified as genuinely active for the listed “Present” date.
A link should be added if the project is public and sufficiently documented.
The project should indicate its scale through usage, contributors, users, or tests where possible.
The broad, promotional claim about AI-first practices should be replaced with a concrete technical contribution or measurable adoption result.
items.because: It is unsupported by measurements and sounds like a general claim rather than evidence of engineering work.

items.says: “Working context” should be defined and its measurement explained.
items.because: The measurement terms are ambiguous.

items.says: The basis of the “100x” raw-conversation growth should be specified as characters, tokens, messages, or another measure.
items.because: The unusually large claim may invite skepticism without a clear definition.

items.says: The 100-turn stress-test setup should be explained enough to establish that it is meaningful.
The effect on cost, latency, task success, or failure rate should be included if measured.
The improvement should be quantified with failure rates, reproduced deadlocks, throughput, or successful fan-out runs.
items.because: The claimed benefit is currently qualitative.

items.says: The bullet should say whether the fix was tested in production, a load test, or a synthetic stress test.
“50-way fan-out” should be defined as concurrent agents, tool calls, requests, or tasks.
The categories or types of the eight metrics should be named.
The bullet should clarify whether the candidate implemented metrics, integrated existing implementations, or built the evaluation interface.
items.because: “Integrated” can describe a wide range of contribution levels.

items.says: The bullet should state whether the work was merged upstream or used by external contributors.
items.because: Open-source adoption or upstream acceptance would strengthen the project.

items.says: The exact Kendall statistical measure and available significance or confidence information should be reported.
The degradation protocol should explain what was removed, how severity was controlled, and what the evaluator score represented.
items.because: The reader must distinguish genuine evaluator validity from correlation caused by the test construction.

items.says: The 400+ trials should be identified as independent reports, repeated runs, or multiple perturbations of the same reports.
items.because: The experimental design is not fully clear.

items.says: The backlog accomplishment appears duplicated from line 14.
items.because: Repeating the same achievement can make the résumé appear padded or inconsistent.

items.says: If this is separate work, the project’s triage branch should be distinguished from the production diagnostics system.
items.because: A project should add new evidence rather than repeat the internship achievement.

items.says: The ownership and timeline of this work should be made explicit.
Git is incorrectly grouped as a programming language.
items.because: Git is a tool rather than a programming language.

items.says: The skills should be organized into categories that distinguish languages, tools, and frameworks.
Substantially used technologies demonstrated in the experience section could be added.
items.because: The skills list should remain defensible rather than include incidental technologies.

items.says: “Agent evaluation” is too broad and should be made more specific.
items.because: The résumé should demonstrate the particular evaluation capabilities intended.

items.says: Central model-serving, data-processing, testing, or infrastructure tools could be added if they are genuinely part of the candidate’s working knowledge.
Anonymized company and university names should be restored on the actual résumé unless confidentiality requires otherwise.
Advanced technical terms should be presented so a non-specialist recruiter can still identify the outcome.
items.because: The résumé currently contains many advanced technical terms.
